title:
Space engineering
Space data links - Telemetry transfer frame protocol
organisation: ECSS Secretariat, ESA-ESTEC Requirements & Standards Division (prepared by the ECSS-E-ST-50-03C Working Group)
status_notes: Second issue (31 July 2008), following ECSS-E-50-03A (6 November 2007); ECSS-E-50-03B was never issued (change log, p. 3). The document itself does not state that it is superseded. The library's later ECSS adoption notices (e.g. ECSS-E-AS-50-25C Rev.1, p. 6) list ECSS-E-ST-50-03C as superseded by ECSS-E-AS-50-22 (CCSDS 132.0-B-x) and ECSS-E-AS-50-23 (CCSDS 732.0-B-x).

key_points.text: A TM Transfer Frame is fixed-length: Primary Header 48 bits, optional Secondary Header 16 to 512 bits, Data Field, optional trailer 16, 32 or 48 bits; maximum frame length 2048 octets, constant per mission phase and sent at a constant rate.
A master channel consists of one to eight virtual channels; all frames on a physical channel share the same Transfer Frame Version Number.

Primary Header fields: Master Channel Identifier 12 bits, Virtual Channel Identifier 3 bits, OCF Flag 1 bit, Master Channel Frame Count 8 bits, Virtual Channel Frame Count 8 bits, Transfer Frame Data Field Status 16 bits.

The Master Channel Identifier is the 2-bit Transfer Frame Version Number (set to '00') plus the 10-bit Spacecraft Identifier (bits 2-11), which is assigned by the CCSDS Secretariat per CCSDS 320.0-B-4 and is static through all mission phases.
With Synchronization Flag '0', the Packet Order Flag is '0' and the Segment Length Identifier is '11' (an obsolete feature marked as not used).
First Header Pointer (bits 37-47): offset of the first packet starting in the data field; '11111111111' if no packet starts in the frame; '11111111110' if the data field contains only idle data.
The Secondary Header is 2 to 64 octets: 8-bit identification (2-bit version '00' and 6-bit length = total length minus one) followed by 8 to 504 bits of mission data.

Extended virtual channel frame count: a 32-bit secondary header (length field = 3) whose 24-bit data field counts roll-overs of the 8-bit VC frame count, giving a 32-bit count. This is not in the CCSDS recommendations.

The Operational Control Field is 4 octets after the data field; Type Flag '0' = Type-1-Report containing a CLCW per ECSS-E-ST-50-04 clause 6.3; Type Flag '1' = Type-2-Report (bit 1 '0' project-specific, '1' reserved).
The Frame Error Control Field (2 octets) is mandatory unless the frame is Reed-Solomon encoded; it uses G(X) = X^16 + X^12 + X^5 + 1 with the shift register preset to all ones.

Compared with ESA-PSS-04-106: PSS allowed 892, 1115 or 1784 octets with RS coding or 128 to 2040 octets without, fixed for the whole mission; this standard allows up to 2048 octets, constant per mission phase.
ESA-PSS-04-106 defined only a 32-bit secondary header and reserved all Type-2 reports; this standard allows 16 to 512 bits and project-specific Type-2 reports.
CCSDS 132.0-B-1 calls a frame with First Header Pointer '11111111110' an OID (Only Idle Data) Transfer Frame; ECSS keeps the meaning but not the term.

Annex D lists the mission configuration parameters: frame length, version number, SCID list, FECF presence, error-frame handling, idle pattern, VCIDs, secondary header and OCF association, synchronization flag, valid packet version numbers, maximum packet length and incomplete-packet handling.

notes: The text extraction uses Unicode non-breaking hyphens (U+2011) in document IDs ('ECSS‐E‐ST‐50‐03C'), so plain-hyphen regex searches can miss them. Figures (frame format, header format, bit numbering) are images and are not in the extracted text. The table of contents lists 'Table B-1' twice (p. 5). Clause 3.1 refers to 'ECSS-ST-00-01' (p. 8), which looks like a typo for the normative reference ECSS-S-ST-00-01. Requirements 5.4.2c/d (p. 24) are truncated in the source ('the Transfer Frame Secondary.'). Clause 5.3.4.1 has the typo 'apply in when' (p. 22). Printed page numbers equal PDF page numbers. PDF page 44 is blank, so srcgrep shows 44 pages while the registry gives 43.
